defects.problem: The first refrain and the following return appear assigned to the wrong audio events. A novelty boundary at 0:58 is not evidence that the first Dunkel refrain occurs there, and the 1:42 G-minor region does not establish Herr dieses Hauses. The first refrain is the G-minor passage at score bars 77–89, followed by the Tempo I ritornello; this report instead puts a sustained G-minor region around 1:45–2:05 and the loud return around 2:10. The present first-refrain/return/host labels are not consistent with that score-and-audio sequence.
defects.evidence: cache/analysis/mahler-das-lied-trinklied.txt: the 0:58/1:28/1:42 boundaries and local-key/loudness windows 0:55–2:25; https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/6/65/IMSLP20582-PMLP47886-Mahler_-_Das_Lied_von_der_Erde_(orch._score).pdf printed pp.11–15; https://musau.org/parts/neue-article-page/view/37 section 3, paragraph 5, identifies refrain 1 as G minor, bars 77–89; https://musau.org/assets/Uploads/2018/Utz/Utz-Mahler-Table04.pdf gives Schuricht’s measured refrain tempo, distinguishing it from Tempo I.
defects.fix: Independently align the first refrain, following Tempo I return and Herr dieses Hauses against the selected Schuricht recording and score; then move the affected section/cue/transition/orchestra anchors together and cite the matching report regions. Investigate the 1:42–2:05 G-minor passage and the loud return around 2:10, rather than treating the earlier novelty peaks as lyric identification. Alternatively make any retained earlier cues feature-only and remove the unestablished refrain/lyric claims at those times. Do not claim an exact lyric entry from a boundary alone.

defects.problem: The text assigns p dolce to the harp patterns, whereas the score and the cue’s own evidence assign dolce to the flutes and clarinets; the first harp is marked p.
defects.fix: Replace ‘two harps play patterns marked p dolce’ with ‘two harps play soft patterns while the flutes and clarinets are marked p dolce’.

defects.problem: The closing climax is called the song’s loudest point, but the report’s loudest window is at 2:20 (−2.9 dB), above 7:40 (−3.1 dB). The evidence correctly describes the loudest closing stretch rather than the whole song.
defects.fix: Replace ‘the song reaches its loudest point’ with ‘the song reaches one of its loudest points’ or ‘the closing stretch reaches its loudest point’.
